title: Cheap Flights From NYC to Europe: JFK & Newark Deals From $329
subtitle: Reykjavik from $329 and London from $349 round-trip, if you book at the right time
airport_names: New York JFK and Newark Liberty (EWR)
meta: Cheap flights from JFK and Newark to Europe: London from $349 on Norse Atlantic, Reykjavik from $329 on Icelandair, Lisbon from $389 on TAP. Here's how to book.

sections.heading: The Prices Worth Chasing From JFK and Newark
sections.body:
Reykjavik on Icelandair from JFK, often from around $329 round-trip, is the cheapest way across the Atlantic from New York. London on Norse Atlantic from JFK comes next, typically from about $349 round-trip. Both are fares you see in the off-season, not in July.

Lisbon on TAP Air Portugal from Newark runs from around $389 round-trip, and Dublin on Aer Lingus from JFK starts at about $399 round-trip. Both fly full-service airlines, so you get a real seat and a meal on the way over. Our pick for most people: Lisbon, because the fare is low and the city is cheap once you land.

Paris on Air France from JFK typically starts around $449 round-trip. That is the most expensive of the five, but it is a legacy carrier with decent service and a short train ride to half of Western Europe.

These are starting prices, not guarantees. Expect to pay more on weekends and around school breaks, and treat any fare in this range as a green light to book.

sections.heading: What the Cheap Fare Actually Gets You
sections.body:
Norse Atlantic and Icelandair both sell a stripped-down base fare. On Norse, the cheapest ticket gets you a seat and a small personal item, nothing more. A carry-on, checked bag, meals and seat selection are all extra.

Add it up and a $349 Norse fare can climb quickly. A carry-on and a checked bag each way often add roughly $100-$200 round-trip, and picking your seat adds more. A $349 ticket can land closer to $500 once you pack a real bag. Always price the full trip before you compare.

Icelandair's lowest fare works the same way, with an economy light ticket that excludes the checked bag and seat choice. Their upside is the free stopover in Iceland, which turns one flight into two destinations for the price of one.

Our rule: if you are traveling with just a backpack, the budget carriers win easily. If you need a checked bag, run the numbers against Aer Lingus or TAP, because the gap shrinks fast and you get meals and a bag allowance on many fares.

sections.heading: When to Fly and When to Book
sections.body:
Winter is the cheap season. January and February fares from New York often run roughly $250-$400 less than peak summer, when round-trips to London or Paris commonly sit around $800-$1,200. The same Lisbon trip that costs about $389 in February can easily double in July.

The shoulder season is the sweet spot if you want better weather without summer prices. Late March and October typically land somewhere between the two, often around $450-$650 round-trip to Dublin, Lisbon or London. October also avoids the biggest crowds.

Transatlantic pricing needs more lead time than domestic flying. For summer, book 3-4 months ahead, which means now if you want July. For off-peak dates, 6-8 weeks out is usually enough.

Set fare alerts the moment you pick your dates. Prices on these routes move in steps, not slowly, and a good fare tends to disappear within a day or two.

sections.heading: Fly Into Lisbon or Dublin, Not Just London
sections.body:
London gets the attention, but Lisbon and Dublin are consistently cheaper to fly into and make excellent bases. Lisbon on TAP from Newark, from around $389 round-trip, puts you in one of Western Europe's cheapest big cities. Meals, transit and hotels cost noticeably less than London or Paris.

From Lisbon, cheap regional flights and trains reach Porto, the Algarve and Spanish cities for well under $100 each way. Our pick: spend two nights in Lisbon, then take the train to Porto.

Dublin on Aer Lingus from JFK, from about $399 round-trip, works the same way. You can clear US preclearance at Dublin on the way home, which saves time at the end of a trip. From there, Ryanair and Aer Lingus connect to the UK and Continental Europe, often for around $30-$80 one-way if you travel light.

The cheapest route to Europe is often not the one that lands in your final city. Book the low fare into Lisbon or Dublin, then add a short budget hop. You usually end up ahead on both price and time.
